utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My microphone is not here. Will you call the case, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: IT-95-16-A, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa appearing for the Prosecution, with Mr. Norman Farrell, and Ms. Adele Erasmus is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Yapa. For the Defence now in the order. Perhaps the Defence could -- could we first have for Zoran Kupreskic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my name is Ranko Radovic, attorney from Zagreb, and I'm Defence counsel for Zoran Kupreskic. I should like to ask you before we begin, go any further that is to say, to solve a technical matter. That technical matter is the following: During the trial so far, we sat in the order of the accused. I was first, then we had my colleague, Ms. Slokovic. Now I see that our colleague, I don't know for what reason, feels that he is entitled to sit in that position, but I would like him to take the position of the Defence counsel for the fourth accused; otherwise, we can consider this to be a discriminating measure of our colleagues from England who feel they are more valuable than his colleagues from Croatia, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a Status Conference, and these things should not really be in our way, so I should like to seek your cooperation for a Status Conference. As you know, it touches upon the matter of procedure. It won't take too long. So, Mr. Radovic, I should like to ask you not to insist on this occasion on this because that would take our time. I should like the procedure to be normal, of course, without any considerations of any discrimination of any kind. That goes without saying. As for the next time, I should like to ask the registrar to see to it that the seating is properly established and determined before the hearing. Mr. Radovic, do you want to add anything to this? Very well, thank you. We shall then proceed with the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am satisfied with your ruling, Your Honour. Let it be as it stands today, but I hope that some order will be introduced into the proceedings next time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The registrar will take note of this. Can we now go on with the appearances, please, on the Defence side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am attorney Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac, and I am Defence counsel for the second accused, Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm Luka Susak. I'm an attorney from Zagreb. I'm Defence counsel for Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Petar Pavkovic, the attorney and Defence counsel for the appellant Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is Livingston, John Livingston. I represent the defendant Vlatko Kupreskic. Can I just say two things? First, is to I apologise for the non-appearance of Mr. Able, who is, of course, leading counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic. He's been unable to attend because of other professional commitments, and he asks me to send his apologies to you in that regard. A second thing is, can I just very briefly say that, of course, no offence was meant to Mr. Radovic by my sitting in the place I am sitting in. I actually sought advice from one of the gentlemen sitting in front of you before I took this position as to whether there were any allotted places. I was told no, and hence I sat at this desk. So I hope that any suggestion of any improper action or taking somebody else's place can be put to rest, and I certainly meant no offence to anybody by doing what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Livingston. Now, I think that this minor incident is closed now, but matter of places assigned to people should be resolved by the registrar before the hearing. This Status Conference is held today in agreement with 65 bis of the rules, and I should like to remind you of its text. It says as follows: "The Appeals Chamber or an Appeals Chamber Judge shall convene a Status Conference within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference, to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise the issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person." It is within that context, within those 120 days, that the Appeals Chamber has convened this Status Conference. There are two items on the agenda. The first one is to take stock of this case which is before the Appeals Chamber, and to ask the parties whether they have any questions to raise in this regard; and the second item, to give the floor to the accused if they wish to say anything, and to inquire after their mental and physical state. So I should like now to ask the accused, first of all, whether they can understand, whether they are following the Status Conference in a language they understand. Do you, therefore, the accused, follow the these proceedings in a language that you can understand? I see that they are nodding their heads which signifies an affirmative answer. Therefore, I should like to remind you, in a very, very few words, where we are and what is the state of affairs in these proceedings. First of all, the Chamber has received the appellants' briefs on the 3rd of July of this year, with the exception of the accused Vlatko Kupreskic's brief which was lodged on the 5th of September on the basis of a decision dated 13th of September, 2000. Then the Chamber decided on the 29th of August to request, on the basis of a decision of the 29th of August, the appellants Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, and Drago Josipovic, to submit, to file, all supplementary evidence which should be attached to the brief pursuant to Rule 115. I should like to remind you that this additional evidence, if there is any, should be addressed pursuant to this decision of the 29th of August, should be addressed to the -- should be submitted to the Appeals Chamber by the 4th of October. And it was only two weeks later after this possible submission of additional evidence, that is, two weeks after that, after this has been filed, if it is filed, that the response needs to be -- is to be filed with the Chamber. And in what is called the book of authorities, a decision of the 7th of September was taken which extended the time, and complete reference, complete documents, should be submitted to the Chamber by the 14th of September, 2000. Regarding the book of authorities, the documents which were submitted on behalf of the accused Vladimir Santic, the Chamber noted that they were incomplete, and I should therefore like to ask the counsel for Vladimir Santic to communicate with the legal advisor, Mr. John Hocking, so that the missing documents could be provided and the whole document completed, the book of authorities completed. So this is the procedure that we have gone through and that I wish to remind you of briefly. Before we move on, I should like to ask the parties if they have any points of procedure they wish to raise today at this Status Conference, and if they do indeed wish to raise anything, will they please do so now. Yes, Mr. Ranko Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In keeping with the orders of the Tribunal, we shall by the 4th of October be supplying and sending in the documents which we have come by. But the Prosecution is very well aware of the fact that all the documents which refer to Ahmici have still not been opened in the state archives of Croatia, so that a review of all the documents and their utilisation will have to be postponed. In the state archives and the reports by the Secret Services of Croatia, they are going through these documents and filing them, and as they have completed a folder, they are handing them over for viewing to the Prosecution and the Defence counsel. I think that so far we have been given insight into only one-third of all the existing documents. So by the 4th of October, we will be able to supply only those documents that we have looked through and set aside, and we will have to look into the additional documents later on because they have only been recently become available and will become available in the near future. That's what I wanted to tell you. That is not our fault because, as you know, it is a state institution, and the state archives, and the archives of the Secret Services, so we'll have to wait for that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Radovic. This is not a new problem. This is not the first time you are raising this matter. It was already raised when you requested an extension of time. Now this deadline has been set, and this is a decision which should be complied with by everybody. Is there anything additional? If there is anything additional, anything that will arrive, that will become accessible to you later on, you can always inform the Chamber and request its authorisation to submit this additional evidence which is of relevance for this case; that is, you will always have the possibility, that is, the possibility which is granted to you by the Statute and the Rules. Yes. Could you please remind me of your name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am counsel Petar Pavkovic, attorney for Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavkovic. And you are here on behalf of Mr. Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to inform Your Honour and to provide Your Honour with an explanation actually. That is to say, the Defence of Mr. Vladimir Santic has met, complied with the requests. We have sent in an index on the 4th of September. On that same day, we sent, via mail, the integral text of our authorities, and all the Defence counsel dispose of those authorities today, and they in the Tribunal. I think the material arrived on the 7th of September. It reached the Tribunal on the 7th of September. So we have fully complied with the Court's request and as the deadline has been pushed forward to the 14th. We sent it by post on the 4th, and the Registry already has received the documents and the Defence counsel have them in their pigeonholes as well. That's what I wanted to tell you will by way of explanation. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Pavkovic. Yes, Mr. Pavkovic. Very well. As I have just said, the mail has arrived, but what I wanted to say at the opening -- will you please stand up, Mr. Pavkovic. Mr. Pavkovic, I'm speaking to you. Will you please stand up. We received the book of authorities with the index, but the document that you are referring to are not complete, and that is why I have to ask you to talk to the legal advisor in the Appeals Chamber, to the legal counsel of the -- legal advisor of the Appeals Chamber and provide them with the documents that are still missing. You need to complete the relevant book of authorities. I should also like to remind you that what we call a book of authorities is not just a list. It is the copies of documents themselves. And the Chamber cannot make copies for you. You have to copy all the documents that you wish to make reference. So all the points on which you are addressing us on then, the whole body of documents that you are referring to, is not in the mail that has reached us. I believe that we have clarified the situation now. Documents need to be supplied too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must be quite frank and say that I did not understand that to be the case, but I will clear up the matter with the Registry, because my learned colleague sitting in front of me, I haven't got all the -- but we'll clarify all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavkovic, it is not all that difficult. You have a list of documents. The list is there but the contents, that is, the documents listed, are not all there in your mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I sent not only a list but the sources as well. What you are saying yourself, a copy of the documents. And my colleague, as a co-counsel, received those documents. Perhaps they're not all there, but we'll clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You will -- if you look at it, you will see that some documents are missing. If they got lost somewhere, then you will supply new copies, Mr. Pavkovic. Very well. Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to Article 65 bis, if the accused wish to raise any matter concerning their physical or mental condition, then they can do so. I am asking the accused. Needless to say any problems that arise in the Detention Unit, of course, have to go through the whole chain of command; that is, they have to be raised first at the Detention Unit. But if you have any other problems that concern your state of health, be it mental or physical, then you're entitled to do so here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: If I might just interrupt for one moment. Just before Your Honour moves on to the defendants, I'm instructed to raise certain matters with you on behalf of Vlatko Kupreskic. I don't know whether this would be a convenient moment for me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please do so. Yes, do so, by all means, Mr. Livingston.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first point is this: that as Your Honour knows, both the appellant's brief and a Rule 115 motion have been filed on behalf of Vlatko Kupreskic. I know the Prosecution have it. I don't know whether my learned friends have it or not, or either of those documents, but they have, as the Court knows, been filed and the time limits have been complied with. As far as this appellant is concerned, we are ready for this appeal to take place. I appreciate, of course, that others have to reply to the documents that we have filed, but Mr. Kupreskic is very anxious indeed that this appeal be heard as speedily as possible, as, of course, are his family who stand behind him. And it is particularly important in his case that this case not be allowed to drift, and one bears in mind that judgement was originally given by the Trial Chamber in the middle of January. Because his sentence is one of six years -- without wishing to prejudge any of the issues on the appeal -- on the worst case scenario, if he lost his appeal, if he lost his sentencing appeal, a two-thirds point in his sentence would be reached at the end of next year. If the sentencing appeal was to succeed to any degree, then the two-thirds point in his sentence would be reached even earlier. If the sentence, for example, were ever to be reduced to five years, if that ever arose, the two-thirds point in his sentence would be April of next year. That is a matter of concern, because it might be that that would be considered his earliest possible date of release. We are, therefore, very anxious that this appeal be progressed and that Mr. Kupreskic do not spend any more time in custody than he need do. I make two constructive suggestions, I hope. The first suggestion is this: that consideration be given today to setting a date, an expedited date, for another Status Conference to thrash out any issues that arise once everybody has reads all the appeal documents, so that a date can be set for this appeal as speedily as possible. And I venture to suggest that on the current timetable, some date in the second half of November might be an appropriate time should the Tribunal be able to accommodate that. The second point is this: that even at this very early date and in order to mitigate any problems there might be about professional -- other professional obligations and in order not to lose any slot that may be available for the Appeals Chamber to hear this case, I would ask Your Honour to consider or to ask that consideration be given even now, provisionally, to pencilling in dates when this appeal could be heard. I appreciate there is a lot of water to go under the bridge before it could be heard but, nonetheless, in the interests of getting the earliest possible slot, which is of concern to the appellant Vlatko Kupreskic, I ask Your Honour to consider that course rather than just let the matter drift and it be fixed sometime next year when other slots that might have been available have been taken up, understandably enough, by other cases. So the main point is we are ready to go. We are not holding up this appeal from being heard. My client is very anxious that it be heard sooner rather than later, and I've indicated certainly one of the principal reasons for that, and I would ask the Court to give real consideration to fixing another Status Conference and to fixing a provisional date, a pencilled-in date for the appeal itself. I think it is possible, because as I know from other cases, time limits are set for submissions on appeals, so it's not as though one is looking at an indefinite period to be set aside to hear this case. Your Honour, unless there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. I do not think there is any need to speak any further on that point. Of course, the decision about the further timetable in the procedure will be taken by the Appeals Chamber, and that is why I interrupted you. I apologise for that. But what is the problem is the evidence itself. The Chamber indeed does what it can to make these cases fair and expedient as possible. So this is our duty, arising from the Statute and from the Rules, to conclude any case as quickly as possible, but the procedure and the schedule has already been set. You will be informed about any further procedure, about any further schedule, and whatever there is to be considered will be considered with the least possible delay. As regards possibly another Status Conference, as the Pre-Appeal Judge and also as the Presiding Judge, we shall notify you with the least possible delay as soon as all the evidence, which is still due, is in the possession, is filed with the Chamber. So as soon as this arrives, you will be informed about that and about the next date with the least possible delay. Do you have anything else to add, Mr. Livingston? I've understood, yes, the drift of your intervention, and there is no need to develop it any further, but if you have any other questions to raise, I'm quite ready to hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LIVINGSTON
utterances.text: I think I've made the points that I wish to make, and I simply wanted the Appeals Chamber to be aware of my client's wish for urgency in dealing with this appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. And please take care that the briefs are filed in time, Mr. Livingston, so that we do not have to make any further decisions on the extensions. Are there any other matters which the parties wish to raise at this stage in the proceedings? I see no sign of this. Therefore, I shall adjourn now. As I have already said, as soon as we receive the evidence that we are expecting from you, that is, in the beginning of the next month, you will be notified about the date of the next Status Conference.
